title: Prompt / Rubric Communication Ablation (Round 2A)
purpose: Test whether the recurring Strong/Partial/Missing calibration errors are materially reduced when the frozen human adjudication rules are communicated more explicitly in the prompt. Tests a causal hypothesis. Pre-ablation wording is HYPOTHESIS_STRENGTHENED, NOT PROMPT_CAUSE_PROVEN.
rules_added: 1. OR / alternative-list semantics (branches are alternatives unless wording requires all; independent qualifiers still apply: years, proficiency, ownership scope, formal work experience, seniority, domain depth)

2. Technology-adjacency guardrail (adjacent tech is not automatic Partial; general LLM/RAG/AI is not automatic credit for multimodal / ASR / RL-training / fine-tuning / training infra / specialised rec-search; else Missing)

3. Project vs formal work experience (a complete project can support Strong for direction/productisation/implementation/delivery; project alone usually cannot support Strong when formal professional-role experience / job-function years / seniority / tenure / full professional ownership is explicitly requested)

4. Compound requirement / narrowest unmet subclaim (judge against the least-supported material subclaim; A AND B needs both strong; one partial subclaim -> Partial; unsupported material subclaim -> possibly Missing; do not split the row)

5. Explicit Strong / Partial / Missing calibration (Strong = direct sufficiently-complete evidence at the requested level; Partial = meaningful but incomplete; Missing = lacking or only general/adjacent; Partial must not be a generic uncertainty bucket)
rules_NOT_added: no Ground-Truth examples, no benchmark cases, no model-specific hints, no Dataset V1 job/requirement ids, no baseline wrong predictions, no per-model failure examples, no score deltas, no benchmark rankings, no new scoring/eligibility/knowledge logic, no company/title heuristics, no candidate-desirability or application-strategy rules
control_source: reused Round 1B same-contract results (Section A + Section D 4-field); NO control rerun
execution_note: kimi-k3 and claude-sonnet-4-5 treatment runs executed in parallel (different providers: Moonshot vs Anthropic; independent per-model latency accounting; no shared rate limit). qwen3.8-max ran first, sequentially.
fixed_contract: Dataset V1, 30 jobs, 100 matchable requirements, Ground Truth V2, frozen candidate evidence, same model ids, same provider transports, same reasoning modes, same temperature policies (kimi temp=1 reasoning_effort=low; qwen temp=0 enable_thinking=false; sonnet temp=0 no thinking), same Section D 4-field output contract, same max_tokens=4096, same one-call-per-job, same normalization (_normalize_matches unchanged), same MatchScoreService, same join key (job_id, requirement_id), same metrics. ONLY the instruction block changed.
transport_normalization_mapping: match_label->match_status, evidence_ids->evidence_source_ids, reason->reason; importance := frozen canonical requirement importance; is_hard_requirement := False + hard_requirement_category := none (v2_matchable); confidence := Medium constant. Unchanged for control and treatment.
contamination_control: raw predictions persisted BEFORE Ground Truth load (guard GROUND_TRUTH_NOT_LOADED_YET on all 90 records). Treatment rules are generic re-statements of the frozen adjudication rubric, not derived from observed individual errors.
success_criteria: clearly successful for a model iff Macro F1 improvement >= +0.05 AND no material grounding degradation AND no catastrophic reliability/coverage loss. Very strong: >= +0.10.

qwen3.8-max.verdict: Not clearly successful. Macro F1 gain negligible; class behaviour shifted (Missing->Partial halved, adjacency FP down) but offset by Partial recall loss and a drop in score-vs-HMF correlation. Compound slice regressed.

kimi-k3.hypothesis_support: WEAKLY_SUPPORTED (classification only) — OFFSET by a coverage regression
kimi-k3.coverage: 100/100 -> 91/100 (1 job `tencent:2047239002926510080` returned empty/non-JSON content under the longer treatment prompt; total_retries 0; single-job, not systematic)
kimi-k3.verdict: Not clearly successful. Per-label calibration on answered requirements improved (Partial F1 +0.078, Partial->Strong inflation -6), but ECC dropped -0.05 from one job losing its output under the longer prompt, and OR-list regressed. The treatment prompt is a RELIABILITY RISK for kimi-k3 and needs a confirming re-run before adoption.

claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929.verdict: Directionally the hypothesis holds best here: Macro F1 +0.032, ECC +0.04, Strong recall +0.077, Missing recall +0.167, OR-list Macro F1 +0.254, adjacency FP -2, Match-Score MAE -2.84, score-vs-HMF +0.032 — all with no coverage/grounding loss. Still below the +0.05 'clearly successful' threshold and still below the quality gate.

cross_model_answers.A_all_three_improve: On Macro F1 all three move positive but small: Sonnet +0.032, kimi-k3 +0.027 (on reconciled), qwen3.8-max +0.013. None reaches +0.05. kimi-k3's gain is offset by a -0.05 ECC coverage regression.
cross_model_answers.B_benefits_most: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (largest Macro F1 gain +0.032, largest ECC gain +0.04, largest OR-list gain +0.254 Macro F1, no downside on coverage/grounding).
cross_model_answers.C_kimi_still_top_quality: On reconciled Macro F1 yes (0.766, still highest). But under the treatment prompt kimi-k3's ECC fell to 0.69 (coverage 91/100) — below qwen3.8-max (0.71) and Sonnet (0.70). Under the CONTROL prompt kimi-k3 is a clean 100/100 at Macro F1 0.740. Top-Quality on classification: yes; on the control prompt only, pending a coverage-confirming re-run of the treatment.
cross_model_answers.D_qwen_max_closes_gap: No. Reconciled Macro F1 gap kimi-qwen widened slightly (0.038 -> 0.052). But qwen3.8-max now leads ECC (0.71 vs kimi 0.69), stays ~2.5x faster and has no reasoning/temperature caveat — so it is a stronger practical option than the raw quality gap implies.
cross_model_answers.E_sonnet_recovers: Partially. +0.032 Macro F1 / +0.04 ECC closes roughly half the distance to qwen3.8-max, but Sonnet stays 3rd of 3 and below the quality gate.
cross_model_answers.F_rule_errors_materially_reduced: Adjacency: YES for 2/3 (qwen3.8-max & Sonnet 0.40->0.80; kimi flat). Project-vs-work: YES for 2/3 (kimi & Sonnet up; qwen3.8-max flat). OR-list: mixed (Sonnet up sharply, qwen3.8-max slightly up, kimi DOWN). Compound: WORSE for all 3 (~0.62 -> 0.54-0.62). Not a clean across-the-board reduction.
cross_model_answers.G_partial_precision_exceeds_060: NO for any model. Best is kimi-k3 treatment 0.571 (from 0.567). Sonnet had the biggest absolute gain (0.462 -> 0.512) but still 0.512. The 0.60 ceiling holds under the treatment prompt.

causal_interpretation: CAUSALLY_SUPPORTED_BUT_SMALL / PARTIAL. The ablation is direct causal evidence that clearer rubric communication shifts model calibration in the predicted direction on specific error types (adjacency FP down 2/3 models; Missing->Partial down for qwen3.8-max and Sonnet; Sonnet OR-list Macro F1 +0.254; Sonnet Strong recall +0.077). The effect on the primary metric (Macro F1) is small (+0.01 to +0.03) and NO model becomes 'clearly successful' (>= +0.05) or clears the quality gate. Compound requirements regressed for all three; kimi-k3 lost coverage. Rubric communication is a REAL, causally-demonstrated, and partially-addressable contributor to the calibration errors, but clearer rubric wording ALONE does not close the gap. NOT claimed as the dominant / sole cause. NOT PROMPT_CAUSE_PROVEN.

post_ablation_recommendation.top_quality: kimi-k3 (control prompt: Macro F1 0.740 / ECC 0.74 / 100 coverage)
post_ablation_recommendation.best_cost_quality: qwen3.8-max (Macro F1 0.70-0.71 either prompt, ECC 0.71, ~2.5x faster, no caveats; unaffected by the rubric)
post_ablation_recommendation.prompt_recommendation: Primary prompt for Dataset V2 = the CONTROL (job-fit-v3-matchable-only). Carry job-fit-v3-rubric-aligned-v1 as a SECONDARY factor to test on Dataset V2 (it helps Sonnet materially, is neutral/slightly-positive for qwen3.8-max, and needs a coverage-confirming re-run for kimi-k3). Do NOT adopt the treatment prompt to production from this task.
